chapters.title: Orchard Core Deployment
chapters.subtitle: Move configuration and content between sites

steps.text: A site is often built in one place and run in another. The Deployment module moves configuration and content between Orchard Core sites. In this video, you build a deployment plan, export a package, and import it on a second site.

chapters.title: Why deployment
chapters.subtitle: The work you repeat by hand

steps.text: You shape a site on one copy, with content types, settings, and pages. When that work is ready, a second site needs the same result. Repeating every change by hand takes time, and a forgotten setting makes the two sites differ.
The Deployment module carries that work in a package. You describe what to include in a deployment plan, run the plan to produce the package, and import the package on the other site.
A package is a zip file that holds a recipe. A recipe is a list of steps, and the destination site runs them in order when you import the package.

Deployment is a feature, listed under Tools, Features. Let's search for Deployment, which shows as Enabled. The Blog recipe enables it, and on a site where it is disabled, an Enable button turns it on.

The Tools, Deployments menu lists Plans, which builds and runs plans, Package Import, which brings in a package, and JSON Import, which runs a recipe that you enter in an editor. Remote Instances and Remote Clients belong to Remote Deployment, which a separate video covers.
This is the source site. Under Settings, General, the Page size is 25. A second site, the staging site, uses a different value, so let's move this setting with a deployment plan.
The Plans page lists the deployment plans of the site, and this site has none. A plan is a named list of steps, so let's select Add Deployment Plan.
A plan needs a name. Let's type Staging Setup and select Create, and the plan opens with no steps in it.
Add Step opens the Available Steps list. Categories on the left group the steps, such as Configuration, Content Management, and Deployment, and each card describes its step.
Modules that export data add their own steps, so the list depends on the enabled features. Let's choose the Configuration category and select Add on the Site Settings card.
The editor lists the site settings, each with a check box. Let's check PageSize and select Create. The plan shows the step, with PageSize as the setting it exports.
Execute opens the Available Targets list. The Deployment module provides File Download, and Remote Deployment adds a target for each remote instance. Let's select File Download.
The browser downloads a zip file named after the plan. It holds the recipe that the steps of the plan produced, so it is ready to import on another site.
This is the staging site, a second Orchard Core site with the Deployment feature enabled. Under Settings, General, its Page size is 10. Let's import the package here.
Under Tools, Deployments, let's open Package Import. The Select a file field accepts a zip package or a recipe file, so let's choose the zip file that the plan produced.
Selecting Import runs the package right away, and the site runs the steps of the recipe in order. The page then shows the message Deployment package imported.
Back under Settings, General, the Page size is 25, the value that the plan exported from the source site.

chapters.title: Permissions
chapters.subtitle: Who can plan, export, and import

steps.text: The Deployment module defines three permissions: Manage deployment plans covers creating and editing plans and their steps, Export Data covers running a plan, and Import Data covers both import pages. The Plans page needs the first two, and administrators have all three.

When you edit a role, Import Data carries a Security Critical badge. A recipe can change settings, features, content definitions, and content, so grant the permission only to roles you trust, and import only packages from sources you trust.
Deployment moves configuration and content between sites: build a plan, export a package, and import it. Separate videos cover plans, imports, and remote deployment in detail. Thanks for watching.
